classification.difficultyReason: Extend the taught regular-polygon rotation pattern to recognise that each vertex gives one matching position, so rotational order equals the number of sides without drawing.

content.prompt:
What are the orders of the rotational symmetry of a regular 36-gon and a regular 37-gon?

Do not attempt to draw them! A regular 36-gon is illustrated to the right, with straight lines between adjacent points.

spec.description: An unlabelled regular 36-gon on a 13-by-13 square grid, with heavier grid lines at three-cell intervals and 36 marked vertices. Straight segments join consecutive vertices; there is no circle, axis or numerical scale.
spec.mathematics: Thirty-six equally spaced vertices, separated by central angles of 10 degrees, joined consecutively.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied illustration; no symmetry order is printed.

answer.worked:
A regular polygon with $n$ sides fits exactly onto itself after each rotation of $\frac{360^\circ}{n}$ about its centre. There are $n$ such positions in a full turn, so its rotational symmetry has order $n$.

The regular 36-gon has order 36, and the regular 37-gon has order 37.
